input.input: text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"gh pr view 75 --json title,body,url,comments; gh pr view 80 --json title,body,url,comments; gh pr view 97 --json title,body,url,files","max_output_tokens":6000}));

content.text:
PR history supports this distinction:

- [PR #75](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/75) separated frontend/backend deployment. It explicitly verified that the frontend Docker target has no Rust-stage dependency.
- [PR #80](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/80) deliberately retained automatic releases containing **all four AMD64 images**, sharing their builds through the composite action. Its scope preserved image targets and cache behavior.
- [PR #97](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/97) changed seven files, all under `frontend/`, and explicitly excluded backend behavior.

Thus frontend-only changes still enter the shared four-image release pipeline. Independent deployment did not introduce selective per-component builds.

No evidence establishes an actual Rust recompilation/cache miss. Invoking the Rust image build can reuse cached compilation layers; logs are needed to distinguish that from compilation.
